summary.tldr: Bans federally regulated employers from using replacement workers during legal strikes or lockouts and makes violations an offence.
what_it_does: Prohibits employers and people acting for them from using replacement workers to do the duties of employees in the bargaining unit during a strike or lockout.
Requires employers to reinstate employees in the bargaining unit, who were on strike or locked out, before any other person when the dispute ends, unless there is a valid reason not to.
Exempts managers, superintendents, supervisors, employer representatives, and some directors or officers from the replacement worker ban.
Allows employers to take necessary steps to prevent the destruction of, or serious damage to, their property.
Makes a breach of the replacement worker rules an offence and sets a fine of up to $10,000 for each day the offence continues.
summary.background: The bill amends the Canada Labour Code rules that apply during strikes and lockouts.
